correctness.rationale: Every parameter, the unwrapped process and variance normalization are defined. Brownian exponential stopping gives an exact bilateral-Laplace law, whose geometric tails produce exact first/second cycle moments. The renewal-reward variance law correctly centers by the clock-correlated velocity, with the last partial cycle negligible at order time. Exponential differentiation gives the mixed moment; a monotonic hyperbolic-ratio argument proves strict sign. A Taylor expansion proves the positive uniform-in-rate first correction for every fixed interior asymmetry, and an exponential bound proves strong-rate collapse. A packaged standard-library checker passed 262 deterministic assertions by independently evaluating sums and mixed moments; finite computation is not offered as proof.

originality.rationale: The 2024 ratchet paper computes exact instantaneous projected current, not the centered macroscopic displacement variance. The 2024 local-resetting paper computes exact nearest-site diffusivity, with which this theorem agrees only at the symmetric-basin specialization; asymmetric basins are not nearest-site projections. Earlier autonomous ratchet and heavy-tail papers analyze physically different substrates or mostly numerical dispersion. Current searches of published research and accessible earlier mathematical claims did not identify a formula equivalent to the asymmetric Poisson clock–jump covariance dispersion or its explicit all-asymmetry weak-rate law. Classical regenerative variance theory is acknowledged and not claimed as new. Inaccessible or unindexed coverage remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The physical gap is the transport dispersion at a nonzero ratchet current, beyond an already computed mean current. The explicit exact biased-projection diffusivity shows a strictly negative covariance correction to a naive independent-mark Poisson model, proves universal weak-rate enhancement with asymmetry-dependent leading coefficient and reveals a finite positive optimal rate (without claiming uniqueness). At asymmetry one quarter and scaled rate eight, diffusivity is about 1.9348 times bare diffusion, beyond the nearest-site lattice benchmark for a mathematically different projector. These are structural quantitative predictions relevant to controlling stochastic transport, not routine restatement of the known symmetric formula.
